# dsh-autocontinue

A dsh plugin that keeps a session working when nobody is watching: it continues
the conversation on

its own, retries through provider and network failures with
backoff, and refuses to let a goal sessi

retries through provider and network failures with
backoff, and refuses to let a goal session stall.
**Version 0.1.13** · verified on `dsh 0.2.1-rc.2`.

## Why

A long unattended run dies in three boring ways: the model stops after one turn
and waits for a huma

n; the uplink drops and the turn ends in `TRANSPORT`; or a
goal quietly loses its activation edge —

the round driver disarms a goal on
error, and a session resume or fork deliberately leaves it disarm

ed. The work is
still perfectly resumable in all three cases. This plugin resumes it.
## What it does
| | Behaviour |
| **Continues** | An armed session's idle agent gets the next round queued for it, instead of waitin

g for a human to type "continue". |
| **Retries** | A turn that failed on the provider or network is
retried forever by default, with exponential backoff that plateaus at a constant 5-minute interval.

|
| **Revives** | A goal that stopped being driven — disarmed after a failure, left disarmed by a r
esume/fork, or paused — is re-armed so the objective keeps moving. |
Nothing runs until a session is **armed** (see Quick start).
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Goal sessions arm themselves (`goalSessions: true`). Profiles that launch
sessions rather than a hum

an — cron, headless, "called in" — set
`enabled: true` and get it for every session in that profile.
## Behaviour
### 1. Continuation

When an armed session's agent goes idle, the plugin queues a round: a normal user
message headed `<a

utocontinue> Round n/…` that tells the model to keep going, to
treat the workspace and tool results

as authoritative, and to end its reply with
the done marker when the assignment is genuinely finishe

d. The transcript reads
as an ordinary conversation.

The loop stops when any of these is true: the model ends a reply with the done
marker (`AUTOCONTINUE

: DONE`), a turn is aborted (you hit stop — a human
interrupt is respected), `maxRounds` is reached,
or you run `/autocontinue off`.
### 2. Retry through outages

Defaults are tuned for an unreliable uplink — retry **forever**, backing off to a
constant 5-minute

are tuned for an unreliable uplink — retry **forever**, backing off to a
constant 5-minute interval:
| Consecutive failure | Wait before the retry |
`maxRetries` is set) |

Each retry round names the exact failure and instructs the model to retry the
action that failed rat

her than restart completed work. Set `maxRetries` to give
up after N, or leave it at `0` to ride out
an outage of any length.
Two implementation facts that matter if you touch this code:

- The retry is driven by `turn/end` with `reason.kind === 'error'` — the turn
boundary that owns a f

ailed request, carrying the harness's structured
`LlmFailure` (`TRANSPORT`, `AUTH`, …).
- `agent/err

or` is deliberately **not** counted. A failed turn emits
`agent/error` first and then `turn/end` wit

h the same failure; counting both
burned two retry credits per outage, so `maxRetries: 2` gave up af

ter a single
real retry. `turn/end` is the only counter.
### 3. Goal revival

A goal stops being driven for reasons unrelated to the objective, and a stalled
goal is worse than a
failed turn because nothing retries it:

- the round driver **disarms** a goal on `agent/error`, so one network blip ends
the goal's own cont

revives work on its own);
- the goal can be **paused**.

With `reviveGoals: true` (default), the plugin calls the sanctioned
`ctx.goals.resume(agent, ref)` —

which carries no caller-authority gate — and the
goal round driver immediately takes the rounds bac

k, keeping the goal's own
round accounting authoritative.
Deliberately **not** revived:

- **`blocked`** — that is the model, or the goal-tool policy, stating the work
cannot proceed. Overr

iding it would fight the harness's own repeated-blocking
policy.
- A goal whose **round budget is sp

ent** — `resume` would throw; `maxGoalRounds`
is the goal's decision to make, not this plugin's.

Revivals are capped by `maxGoalRevives` (default 5) so something that keeps
pausing a goal cannot pi

ng-pong with it forever; the counter resets as soon as
the goal actually starts a round. Every reviv
al is announced in the chat.
### 4. Restart recovery

A server swap (the `dsh-update` staged install + reload) or a crash stops the
process while a turn i

s still open: the persisted log ends inside `turn/start`
with no `turn/end`, and no live agent is le

ft to continue it. On startup this
plugin scans the session corpus, and for every recently-written l

og that still
ends inside a turn it reopens the session through the same path the Web GUI uses
(`res
olveAgent`) and queues a resume round.
That does three things the browser cannot be relied on for:

- the harness appends its synthetic `interrupted` closers, so the old turn is
balanced instead of lo

oking like a permanently running one;
- the session's agent preset and model selection are recompose

ab still continue, which is what keeps a switch from
orphaning work in another workspace.

The resumed session is told exactly what happened so it does not spend a round
working it out: the n

otice and the resume round name the durable cut
(`turn N, step M`), say the interruption was infrast

ructure — an update or a
crash — rather than a verdict on the plan, and tell the model not to invest

igate
it or re-plan from scratch. A goal session gets the same explanation as an
